subject: On‑prem keystore & operator access — evidence & routing questions
messages:
From: Lara Kent <lara.kent@heliohealth.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on on‑prem keystore and operator evidence

Rohan — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement flagged a few items in the DPA redline that need clarification before legal will sign. High level asks: can you confirm operator access patterns for our on‑prem deployment (VPC + air‑gapped option), how customer keys are handled (BYOK vs escrow), and what audit evidence Redwood can provide for operator activity and data egress?

Specifically:
- If we provide a CMK (customer‑managed key), does Redwood ever hold or be able to export the plaintext key?
- What breakglass/forensics process exists for emergency support and how is that logged?
- Which subprocessors (if any) will have access to telemetry or logs in the private deployment model? We need company names and locations for our data transfer/DPAs.

I attached the redline with inline notes. Can you loop in security/ops? We want to land this quickly but need these items cleared.

Thanks,
Lara Kent
Head of Compliance, HelioHealth
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Lara Kent <lara.kent@heliohealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on on‑prem keystore and operator evidence

Lara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, followed by a proposal for evidence and a request for any jurisdictional constraints you have (e.g., EU data residency, onshore subprocessors).

High level answers:
- BYOK: Redwood never stores customer plaintext keys. For Private deployments we support customer‑managed keys (CMKs) where the key material remains under your control (HSM/KMS in your VPC or provided HSM on‑prem). We can support a keystore connector; our operator processes cannot export key material.
- Escrow: we offer an optional sealed‑escrow mechanism for customer approval cases — escrow only occurs with explicit signed authorization and uses an encrypted envelope split across two vaults; we can supply a notarized procedure if required.
- Breakglass: emergency access is allowed via an auditable breakglass workflow that requires multi‑party signoff (customer ops + Redwood oncall) and is recorded to immutable audit logs retained for 7 years by default (adjustable).
- Subprocessors: for Private deployments the default is no Redwood subprocessors with access to customer data. If any vendor components are used (e.g., hardware support partners), we disclose the names and locations up front and include them in the DPA as subprocessors.

Evidence we can provide (proposed):
1) Operator activity logs (immutable) with redaction options — sample CSV and audit timeline.
2) HSM proof-of‑possession: challenge/response proof that keys are only resident in customer HSM (no plaintext export).
3) Architecture diagram showing network egress controls and operator jump‑host boundaries.
4) Signed statement of subprocessors and their jurisdictions.

Irene and Kim — any concerns or additions before I send this to Lara + legal? I attached a short diagram and our proposed evidence checklist.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: Lara Kent <lara.kent@heliohealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on on‑prem keystore and operator evidence

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from security ops:
- For BYOK in a VPC we run a connector pattern that performs remote attestation; the connector never sends key material back to Redwood. Logs include KMS usage records (encrypt/decrypt calls).
- For on‑prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 and provide an agent that only exposes signing/encryption operations; the agent is one‑way and we can provide a signed attestation of the agent binary and configuration.
- We will provide a sanitized sample of the immutable operator audit logs (timestamps, operator id hashes, activity code) and a playbook showing how breakglass requests are initiated/approved.

I recommend adding a short clause in the DPA: "Customer keys are not exportable by Redwood and operator access to key material is prohibited except under documented, customer‑authorized breakglass scenarios." If legal wants stronger language we can draft specific binding operational commitments.

I can produce the attestation package and a 2‑page runbook for HelioHealth by Monday.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lara Kent <lara.kent@heliohealth.com>, rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on on‑prem keystore and operator evidence

Lara — thanks, wanted to call out two legal items we typically see in DPAs for private deployments:
1) Subprocessor list timing: we provide a snapshot list at signing, and we will notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days prior to onboarding with an opt‑out break (ability to terminate the SOW instead of consent). For HelioHealth we can commit to onshore subprocessors only (US) for this engagement.
2) Data transfer: for on‑prem/VPC there is no cross‑border data transfer unless HelioHealth requests monitoring or support that routes logs outside the region; any such action requires explicit written consent and will be limited to aggregated telemetry by default.

Attached is a redline suggestion for the clause Irene recommended and a sample notification template for subprocessor changes. Once Lar a confirms, we can update the DPA and push to DocuSign.

— Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Lara Kent <lara.kent@heliohealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 16:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on on‑prem keystore and operator evidence

Team — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow ups before we execute:
- Please attach the HSM attestation package (Irene) and the sanitized audit‑log sample (Irene) to the DPA record.
- For the escrow option: we need the exact escrow process (who holds each vault, what legal mechanism unseals, and which jurisdictions apply). Can you add that as an annex rather than inline?
- Subprocessor commitment to US‑only is a condition for HelioHealth. If Redwood accepts, procurement will move forward this week.

If you can attach the two artifacts and a short annex describing escrow custody (and confirm DocuSign link), I will circulate to Legal & Procurement for final sign.

Regards,
Lara
Head of Compliance, HelioHealth
